```{python}
#| label: d5-setup
#| code-summary: "Chapter setup"
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from mdmx import artifacts, data, latex, lifetable, plotting, provenance
from mdmx.config import params

provenance.start_chapter("d5-pooling")
plotting.use_style()
P = params()
cur = artifacts.load("lt_curated")
lt_cur = cur["lt"]
de = artifacts.load("hmd_raw")["de"]
labels = artifacts.load("event_labels")
pops = artifacts.load("populations")
names = dict(zip(pops["code"], pops["name"]))
```

## The problem: zeros in small populations

Between late childhood and middle age, the annual probability of dying is
of the order of $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-3}$.  In a population the size of Iceland
or Luxembourg that means a handful of deaths — or none — at each single age
in a given year.  When the HMD records no deaths, $m_x$ and $q_x$ are
exactly zero, and their logit is $-\infty$ (in practice, the floor
$\operatorname{logit}(10^{-8}) \approx -18.4$, far below any real value
near $-7$).  Left in the tensor, such cells are enormous outliers that the
decomposition would spend rank on.

## The remedy: pool adjacent years

Following @clark2001investigation, we pool adjacent years: deaths and
exposures are summed over a block of years and the pooled rate
$m_x = \sum_t D_{x,t} / \sum_t E_{x,t}$ replaces the single-year rates.  A
block is just wide enough to contain at least one death at every affected
age, so large populations are not pooled at all and small ones only as much
as they need.  The algorithm, implemented in
`mdmx.data.adaptive_pooling()`, is:

1. **Valley ages.**  Ages whose median $q_x$ across all populations, sexes
   and years is below $q_{\text{thresh}} =$ `{python} P.data.valley_q_threshold`.
2. **Flag.**  A population–sex is pooled only if one of its non-exceptional
   years has $m_x = 0$ at a valley age.  Its *pooling ages* are the valley
   ages plus any other age below `{python} P.data.pool_raw_rate_age_limit` at which it
   has a zero rate (in the very smallest populations zeros also occur a few
   years above the valley).  Above that age the HMD's rates are smoothed by
   a model and are never zero.
3. **Blocks.**  The flagged population–sex's non-exceptional years are
   taken in calendar order and split into *runs* wherever more than
   `{python} P.data.pool_max_gap` calendar years are missing (so 2019 and 2023 belong to
   the same run across the COVID years 2020–22, but a long gap breaks the
   run).  Within a run, years are added to a block until every pooling age
   has at least one death in the block; the block is then closed and the
   next begins.  Years left over at the end of a run join the previous block.
4. **Pool and rebuild.**  In a block of two or more years, the pooled rate
   $\sum_t D_{x,t}/\sum_t E_{x,t}$ is computed at each pooling age, and in
   every year of the block $q_x$ at those ages is recomputed from the pooled
   rate and that year's own $a_x$: $q_x = m_x / \{1 + (1-a_x)\,m_x\}$.
5. **Everything else is untouched.**  Outside the pooling ages, every year
   keeps the HMD's published $q_x$; single-year blocks (years that already
   have deaths at every pooling age) and unflagged populations are not
   changed at all; and exceptional years are never pooled.

```{python}
#| label: d5-pool
#| code-summary: "Find the valley ages and pool (cached)"
def _pool():
    valley = data.valley_ages(lt_cur, P.data.valley_q_threshold)
    pooled, blocks = data.adaptive_pooling(
        lt_cur, de, labels, valley,
        max_gap=P.data.pool_max_gap, raw_rate_age_limit=P.data.pool_raw_rate_age_limit)
    return {"lt": pooled, "blocks": blocks, "valley_ages": valley}

res = artifacts.stage("lt_pooled", _pool, inputs=["lt_curated", "hmd_raw", "event_labels"],
                      params=P.section("data"),
                      code=[_pool, data.valley_ages, data.adaptive_pooling, data.plan_blocks,
                            data.contiguous_runs, lifetable.qx_from_mx],
                      desc="Life tables after adaptive temporal pooling, with the block record")
lt_pool, blocks, valley = res["lt"], res["blocks"], res["valley_ages"]
print(f"Valley ages: {valley.min()}–{valley.max()}")
print(f"Multi-year blocks: {len(blocks)} in {blocks.groupby(['pop', 'sex']).ngroups} population-sexes "
      f"({blocks['pop'].nunique()} populations)")
print(f"Country-years pooled: {int(blocks['n_years'].sum())} (sex-specific)")
print(f"Block width: median {blocks['n_years'].median():.0f}, max {blocks['n_years'].max()} years")
latex.report("dataValleyFirst", int(valley.min()), text=str(int(valley.min())), desc="First valley age")
latex.report("dataValleyLast", int(valley.max()), text=str(int(valley.max())), desc="Last valley age")
latex.report("dataNPoolBlocks", len(blocks), desc="Multi-year pooling blocks")
latex.report("dataNPoolPops", blocks["pop"].nunique(), desc="Populations with at least one pooled block")
latex.report("dataNPoolYears", int(blocks["n_years"].sum()), desc="Sex-specific life tables changed by pooling")
latex.report("dataPoolMaxWidth", int(blocks["n_years"].max()), desc="Widest pooling block (years)")
latex.report("dataPoolMedianWidth", int(blocks["n_years"].median()), desc="Median pooling block width (years)")
latex.report("dataValleyQThreshold", P.data.valley_q_threshold, text=f"{P.data.valley_q_threshold:g}",
             desc="Valley ages: median q_x below this threshold")
latex.report("dataPoolMaxGap", int(P.data.pool_max_gap), desc="Most missing years a pooling run may span")
```

```{python}
#| label: d5-blocks
#| code-summary: "Blocks per population, and the widest blocks"
per_pop = (blocks.groupby("pop").agg(blocks=("n_years", "size"), years=("n_years", "sum"),
                                     widest=("n_years", "max"))
           .sort_values("years", ascending=False))
per_pop.index = per_pop.index.map(names)
display(per_pop)
blocks.sort_values("n_years", ascending=False).head(10)
```

The widest blocks belong to the smallest populations — Iceland, the Māori
population of New Zealand, Northern Ireland, Estonia and Luxembourg — where
a block of a decade or more is needed before every single age between 1
and the late forties has recorded a death.  Because only the zero-prone
ages are pooled, these long blocks do not flatten the trend in infant or
old-age mortality, which carry most of the information about the level of
mortality in each year.

## What pooling does to the schedules

```{python}
#| label: fig-s2-smoothing
#| fig-cap: "Single-year versus pooled schedules (logit q_x, females) for four small populations. Thin grey lines: the published single-year schedules of the years in one block; blue line: the pooled result for one year of the block. Orange shading marks the pooling ages. Outside them the schedules are unchanged."
SHOW = ["ISL", "LUX", "EST", "NZL_MA"]
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(10, 7), sharex=True)
for ax, pop in zip(axes.flat, SHOW):
    b = (blocks[(blocks["pop"] == pop) & (blocks["sex"] == "female")]
         .sort_values("n_years").iloc[len(blocks[(blocks["pop"] == pop) & (blocks["sex"] == "female")]) // 2])
    years = [int(y) for y in b["years"].split()]
    for y in years:
        s = lt_cur[(lt_cur["pop"] == pop) & (lt_cur["sex"] == "female") & (lt_cur["year"] == y)]
        ax.plot(s["age"], lifetable.logit(s["qx"], P.data.q_min), color="#bbbbbb", lw=0.6)
    s = lt_pool[(lt_pool["pop"] == pop) & (lt_pool["sex"] == "female") & (lt_pool["year"] == years[0])]
    ax.plot(s["age"], lifetable.logit(s["qx"], P.data.q_min), color=plotting.COLORS["respiratory"], lw=1.8)
    changed = (lt_pool.set_index(["pop", "sex", "year", "age"])["qx"]
               != lt_cur.set_index(["pop", "sex", "year", "age"])["qx"]).loc[(pop, "female", years[0])]
    ages_changed = changed[changed].index.to_numpy()
    if len(ages_changed):
        ax.axvspan(ages_changed.min() - 0.5, ages_changed.max() + 0.5, color="#fdae61", alpha=0.25)
    ax.set_ylim(-19, 0)
    ax.set_title(f"{names[pop]}, {b['first']}–{b['last']} ({b['n_years']} years)", fontsize=10)
for ax in axes[1]:
    ax.set_xlabel("Age")
for ax in axes[:, 0]:
    ax.set_ylabel(r"logit$(q_x)$")
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s2-smoothing")
plt.show()
```

How much noise does pooling remove?  A good measure is the year-to-year
change in $\operatorname{logit}(q_x)$ at each age: real mortality changes
slowly, so large jumps between consecutive years are mostly noise.  The
figure compares the median absolute year-to-year change, before and after
pooling, over the *same* country-years (all non-exceptional years of the
pooled populations, zero-free cells only so that the floor does not dominate
the "before" curve).

```{python}
#| label: fig-s2-smoothing-by-age
#| fig-cap: "Median absolute year-to-year change in logit(q_x), by age, before (grey) and after (blue) pooling, over the same non-exceptional country-years of the pooled populations. Cells with a zero rate before pooling are excluded from both curves."
pooled_ps = set(map(tuple, blocks[["pop", "sex"]].drop_duplicates().to_numpy()))
nonexc = labels.loc[labels["label"] == 0, ["pop", "year"]]
def yearly_change(lt):
    df = lt.merge(nonexc, on=["pop", "year"])
    df = df[[ (p, s) in pooled_ps for p, s in zip(df["pop"], df["sex"])]].copy()
    df["z"] = lifetable.logit(df["qx"], P.data.q_min)
    df = df.sort_values(["pop", "sex", "age", "year"])
    g = df.groupby(["pop", "sex", "age"], observed=True)
    df["dz"] = g["z"].diff().abs()
    df["consecutive"] = g["year"].diff() == 1
    return df.set_index(["pop", "sex", "age", "year"])
before, after = yearly_change(lt_cur), yearly_change(lt_pool)
ok = before["consecutive"] & (before["qx"] > 0) & (before.groupby(level=[0, 1, 2]).shift(1)["qx"] > 0)
med_before = before.loc[ok, "dz"].groupby(level="age").median()
med_after = after.loc[ok[ok].index, "dz"].groupby(level="age").median()
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4.5))
ax.plot(med_before.index, med_before.to_numpy(), color=plotting.COLORS["grey"], lw=1.6, label="Before pooling")
ax.plot(med_after.index, med_after.to_numpy(), color=plotting.COLORS["respiratory"], lw=1.6, label="After pooling")
ax.axvspan(valley.min() - 0.5, valley.max() + 0.5, color="#fdae61", alpha=0.2, label="Valley ages")
ax.set_xlabel("Age"); ax.set_ylabel(r"median |Δ logit$(q_x)$| between consecutive years")
ax.legend()
plotting.save_figure(fig, "fig-s2-smoothing-by-age")
plt.show()
valley_mask = med_before.index.isin(valley)
reduction = 1 - med_after[valley_mask].mean() / med_before[valley_mask].mean()
latex.report("dataPoolNoiseReduction", 100 * reduction, digits=0,
             desc="Percent reduction in median year-to-year |Δlogit q| at valley ages, pooled populations")
print(f"Year-to-year noise at valley ages reduced by {100 * reduction:.0f}%")
```
